summary_for_children: Al-Haqqah means The Reality. It recalls peoples who denied the truth, like 'Ad, and speaks of the Day of Judgement only in its own words.
environment_concept: A windswept valley (69:6) with hollow palm trunks lying fallen (69:7).

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Certain Reality
story_library.children_narration: Surah Al-Haqqah reminds us that the Day of Judgment is real. It recalls communities that rejected guidance and asks us to think about our actions. Our choices matter, even when no one else seems to notice them.

world_idea.title: The Great Reflection Hall
world_idea.description: Travel through atmospheric landscapes connected to narrated lessons from past communities. Use an interactive journal to reflect on everyday actions without attempting to depict the unseen judgment.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: No judgment scenes; past peoples are readings only.
